issues.description: The Meal constructor parameter order in the template does not match the problem specification UML, the example usage in Main, nor the solution. The template declares Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) while the UML and solution (and Main's example) expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients). This will cause compile-time confusion/errors when students use the constructor as shown in the problem and Main.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Meal constructor in the template to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) so its parameter order matches the UML in the problem statement, the example usage in Main, and the solution. Alternatively, if the reversed order was intentional, update the problem statement and Main examples to use the template's constructor signature consistently.

issues.description: The Meal constructor signature differs between the problem statement / solution and the template. The UML and solution expect Meal(String, String[]) (name first, then ingredients), and the example usage in Main also constructs Meal with (String, String[]) — but the template's Meal.java declares the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (parameters reversed). This mismatch will confuse students and cause an API/usage inconsistency (and potential compilation or runtime errors) when they follow the problem description or the example Main code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Meal constructor match the problem statement and solution by changing its signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and adjust the constructor body accordingly (assign name to this.name and ingredients to this.ingredients). This aligns the API with the UML, the example usage in Main, and the solution implementation.
